hits.name: Boris Cherny
hits.text: Tag writes >50% of my PRs every day. It also does ~100% of my data analysis, and fixes most of our product feedback + bugs. It's not like a regular Slack bot. It is proactive, programmable, it has memory, it has access to your connectors. With Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1, it has strong judgement. Example prompts I use: - "@Claude react to threads in this channel with ✅ when resolved" - "@Claude from now on, attempt to repro every bug in this channel end to end, running the full app. once you reproduce the bug, put up a pr to fix it and tag the right team for code review" - "@Claude brainstorm ~100 hypotheses for what could explain this weird data, use a workflow to in/validate. spend 10m tokens or so digging very deep. draw a chart with the result." - "@Claude make me an interactive game explaining how this part of the code works, then make a slide deck explaining it for others on the team" https://t.co/gmsALM8Lvs
hits.video_tip: 20s: Slack thread → @agent prompts → PR opened montage → proactive coworker.
hits.hook: Tag agent >50% of PRs + copyable prompts - agent-as-coworker bible.

hits.name: Matt Pocock
hits.text: I hear this a LOT from panic-stricken devs: "I've inherited a vibe-coded codebase, how do I save it?" Either from devs who have stopped caring, or non-technical folks trying to push AI beyond their abilities. A huge chunk of my next course will tackle this: - deepening modules - establishing domain language - increasing testability - explaining non-obvious code with ADR's - automated code migrations

hits.name: Matt Pocock
hits.text: Tons of folks ask me "how do I create a CODING_STANDARDS.md file?" My answer is that if you're using it right, it should only be empty for about 5 minutes. Every meaningful thing your agent gets wrong should be noted into CODING_STANDARDS. - Forget to implement dark mode? - Forgot a validation rule? - Used the wrong framework primitive? Use /retro to fill it up, or modify it yourself.
hits.video_tip: 12s: empty md → agent mistake flash → bullet appears → file growing.
hits.hook: CODING_STANDARDS.md fills from agent mistakes - harness habit.

hits.name: claire vo 🖤
hits.text: My (hard earned) opinion on public vs private vs whatever is ultimately it comes down to admin + teachers + standards, and in no school do you get to choose your admin or teachers or standards (you get what you get and you don't get upset.) So if you can, my advice is to leave yourself as much budget and time to teach your kids yourself or supplement with instruction you choose to fill in gaps, because no matter what: you will find gaps. They will maybe show up every year, or be bigger one year than the other. These are human systems with human problems--you have to be the net. I've ultimately found that our kids academic performance is a reflection of our family values, how we spend our time, and what we expect from the kids. School can support or accelerate it, but at the end of the day we hold the job as parents. Lucky to have the time and resources to do it, so we make it a priority. This has been something @elawless has built into our family system, and I'm deeply grateful.
hits.video_tip: 12s: school hallway → parent+kid homework table → you are the net.
hits.hook: You are the net - standards over school brand.

We’re building Copilot as a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task. Today, we’re announcing our biggest update to Copilot to date, bringing four things together:

· Autopilot: proactive and long-running agent built for the enterprise
· Code: build apps with Copilot, hosted inside your company’s tenant
· Home: Chat + Cowork together
· Office: now fully embedded in Copilot (and Copilot embedded in Office, of course!)

Plus, you can invoke Copilot in Teams, and we’re introducing Today, a proactive experience that surfaces the most important information from across M365 without needing to ask for it.

The way we work is changing and so are our workflows. This update brings AI into that flow, from answering a question, to building an app, to getting work done on your behalf.
